results.name: Eswatini
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the men were sent to Eswatini by the United States, but they are being held by Eswatini. Amnesty International reported on 16 July 2026 that at least 30 men transferred under the arrangement remain at Matsapha maximum-security prison without charge and denied confidential access to a lawyer, five of them for a full year.

results.name: Vanuatu
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Vanuatu won a legal argument its people cannot yet drink, switch on or shelter behind. Commentary on 24 July 2026 found the International Court of Justice victory has not produced repaired water systems, restored electricity or coastal protection, but that gap is already carried in the score and produced no movement.

results.name: Niger
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Niger answered a request for release by changing the law. Human Rights Watch reported on 23 July 2026 that a week after Moussa Tiangari’s lawyers applied for his release, the authorities extended maximum pretrial detention to four years, renewable once.

results.name: Uganda
results.key_finding: Why it matters: in Uganda the army is being used against the people who challenge it in court. Human Rights Watch reported on 16 July 2026 that at least five critics have been unlawfully seized since mid-June, and that since 28 June the military has laid siege to Nation Media Group, the country’s largest independent media company.

results.name: Dhaka
results.key_finding: Why it matters: most of the deaths that flagged Dhaka did not happen in Dhaka. The floods killed at least 44 people in the southeast, several hundred kilometres away, so the attribution rule applies; what counts is that police baton-charged students protesting exams held during the floods.

results.name: Kathmandu
results.key_finding: Why it matters: in Kathmandu the people who went to check on flood victims ended up in custody. Police detained three activists on 11 July 2026 after they visited a holding centre for families displaced by forced evictions, and Majid Ansari spent five days in hospital and was still held on 15 July.

results.name: Kuala Lumpur
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the demand that flagged Kuala Lumpur was aimed at the wrong capital. The Migrant Welfare Network letter of 15 July 2026 was addressed to Bangladesh’s head of government, not Malaysia’s, though the documented debt bondage and passport confiscation happen on the Malaysian side of the corridor.

results.name: Addis Ababa
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the harm protested in Addis Ababa was not done by Addis Ababa. Thousands rallied at Meskel Square on 18 July 2026 against abductions and forced recruitment attributed to authorities in Tigray, hundreds of kilometres north, so the attribution rule prevents it from lowering the city’s score.

results.name: Tunis
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Tunis has never actually been assessed. Its published 34.4 is the same un-assessed seed Tunisia the country carried before evidence was gathered, and thousands marched down Habib Bourguiba Avenue on 25 July 2026 demanding President Kais Saied resign after five years of rule by decree.

results.name: Johannesburg
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the attacks were not carried out by the city, but keeping the clinic doors open was the city’s job. An anti-migrant group blocked foreigners from public clinics west of Johannesburg while Nigeria evacuated 1,490 of its citizens between 10 June and 15 July 2026.

results.name: Hong Kong
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Hong Kong handled a real storm well, and that is not the same as a change in how it treats people. Typhoon Noul made landfall on 26 July 2026, the government opened 29 shelters and published same-day situation reports, but one well-run hazard event is not a structural improvement.

results.name: Boston Dynamics
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the first strike in history against a humanoid robot happened on the day Boston Dynamics changed hands. Hyundai closed its full acquisition on 20 July 2026 and 35,000 Ulsan workers escalated a strike demanding written guarantees before any Atlas robot enters a Korean production floor.

results.name: Unitree Robotics
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the headline that flagged Unitree carried the wrong date. The Pentagon added Unitree to its Chinese Military Companies list on 8 June 2026, not 20 July, and a second claim about the G1 transmitting sensor data to Chinese servers had no dated source and was dropped.

results.name: Apple
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Apple is trying to settle rather than fight, and that is not the same as fixing anything yet. Bloomberg reported on 17 July 2026 that Apple and the US Department of Justice are in early talks to settle the 2024 iPhone antitrust case, with no trial date set.

results.name: Florida
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Florida has executed more people this year than every other state combined, and it also leads the country in death row exonerations. It carried out 10 executions by mid-July 2026, and Dennis Sochor on 15 July was the 29th person put to death in 19 months.

results.name: A.O. Smith
results.key_finding: Why it matters: no news is itself a finding, and rotation checks are where quiet decisions surface. A.O. Smith filed a WARN notice on 23 June 2026 to close two central Ohio plants and cut 92 jobs effective 24 August, a pre-window event that does not count as in-window conduct.

results.name: ADP
results.key_finding: Why it matters: no news is itself a finding. ADP was assessed on rotation with no in-window evidence; the nearest relevant event is a June 2026 class settlement covering roughly 50,000 people over retirement-plan fees, which is the strongest accountability signal available.

results.name: Agilent Technologies
results.key_finding: Why it matters: no news is itself a finding, and two workforce claims were dropped for lack of a date. Agilent reproduces its published 77.9 exactly; reported Biovectra subsidiary cuts and repeated 1 to 3 per cent annual reductions could not be tied to any dated statement and were not scored.

results.name: Aon
results.key_finding: Why it matters: a risk company took more than 14 months to find a breach inside itself. Aon settled a class action for 1.5 million dollars over a data breach that ran from 29 December 2020 to 5 March 2022, which holds its blind-spot and anticipatory-awareness scores below anchor 4.

results.name: Citigroup
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the scanner reported no evidence for Citigroup, and there was some. On 24 July 2026 a New York federal judge sent former employees’ wage claims to arbitration, meaning the question of whether the bank required inaccurate time reporting will not be answered in public.

notes: BACKFILL RUN. This is the assessor stage for the 2026-07-26 night, reconstructed on 2026-07-27. assessment_date is 2026-07-26 in every artifact. No digest, no briefings, no index writes, no proposal applications. DATE DISCIPLINE. No evidence dated after 2026-07-26 was scored, cited or referenced. Every score-moving numeric claim was checked against a dated statement in the source itself, not only against the source URL. Background sources older than the 2026-07-12 to 2026-07-26 window are used only for standing structural context and are labelled with their true dates. CLAIMS DROPPED OR CORRECTED ON DATE-VERIFICATION GROUNDS. Six. (1) UNITREE ROBOTICS: the scan placed the Pentagon flagging of Unitree as Chinese military-linked technology on 20 July 2026. That is the TechTimes article date. The Department of Defense added Unitree (Hangzhou Yushu Technology) to the Section 1260H list on 8 June 2026, corroborated by TechCrunch of 8 June 2026 and a WilmerHale client alert of 11 June 2026. Re-dated to background, out of window. (2) UNITREE ROBOTICS: the scan claim that research found the G1 humanoid continuously transmitted sensor data to Chinese servers could not be tied to any dated source. Dropped entirely rather than inferred. (3) KUALA LUMPUR: the scan stated the Migrant Welfare Network urged the Malaysian government to negotiate a binding bilateral labour agreement. The Daily Star and The Business Standard both show the letter was addressed to Bangladesh’s head of government ahead of a state visit to Malaysia. Attribution corrected before scoring. (4) TUNIS: the scan dated the rally 26 July 2026. Al Jazeera, published 26 July, states the march took place on Saturday, which was 25 July 2026. Event re-dated; both dates remain inside the window. (5) BOSTON DYNAMICS: the prior assessment of 2026-07-22 recorded the Hyundai acquisition as completing on 16 July 2026. Multiple dated sources place the closing on 20 July 2026, the contractual deadline for SoftBank to exercise its put option; the June transaction was the purchase of the remaining 9.65 per cent stake. Corrected. (6) AGILENT TECHNOLOGIES: reported Biovectra subsidiary staff cuts in Prince Edward Island and Nova Scotia, and reported annual reductions of 1 to 3 per cent for three consecutive years, carry no verifiable date. Not scored; recorded as an evidence gap. FIGURE MOVEMENT RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED BY INFERENCE. Two. DHAKA: flood death tolls ranged from 44 (Reuters, 11 July 2026) to 51 (later national reporting). The lower, better-corroborated dated figure was used. HONG KONG: injury and fallen-tree counts differ across sources because they are snapshots taken at different hours on 26 July 2026 (18 injured / 153 trees at one point, 188 trees and a higher count at another). Each figure is attributed to the report that carried it rather than reconciled into a single headline number. GATE WARNINGS RESOLVED. Both. ESWATINI: the Amnesty document AFR 55/1270/2026 carries no verifiable date component in its URL. It is not carrying the flag alone; a dated IOL report of 9 July 2026 independently establishes the arrival of 11 deportees and the fourth phase of the arrangement, and the one-year anniversary framing places the Amnesty publication at 16 July 2026. FLORIDA: the superlative claim (most executions since the 1976 reinstatement, record pace) was corroborated against Florida Phoenix of 15 July 2026, WMNF of 16 July 2026 and the Death Penalty Information Center Florida record before scoring. The Washington Times item flagged as undated was excluded and not used. The scanner’s deliberate exclusion of the two executions scheduled for 28 July 2026 was preserved; no future-scheduled execution is scored or referenced as completed. CHANGE PROPOSALS. Three, all filed with status pending and none applied to any published index. (1) TUNIS, published 34.4, assessed 22.5, delta -11.9, recommendation downgrade, confidence medium. First evidence-based baseline: rotation-state records last_assessed null and the published 34.4 is numerically identical to the un-assessed seed Tunisia the country carried before its own first assessment on 2026-07-10. No band crossing (34.4 and 22.5 are both Developing), and sourcing exceeds the band-crossing bar anyway with a tier-5 OHCHR press release, a tier-3 HRW analysis inside the window and two tier-2 wire reports. The assessed 22.5 sits within a point of Tunisia the country’s own most recent assessment of 23.1 on 2026-07-24. (2) UGANDA, published 20.3, assessed 13.1, delta -7.2, recommendation flag-for-review, confidence medium. Evidence is real and negative: HRW of 16 July 2026 on at least five critics unlawfully seized since mid-June and the military siege of Nation Media Group from 28 June. However the move crosses a band label and the band-crossing bar requires at least two distinct sources with at least one at sourceTier 4 or above; the strongest in-window source is HRW at tier 3, and the tier-5 UN Secretary-General note is dated 2 July 2026, outside the window. Routed for human judgment rather than asserted as a downgrade. (3) KATHMANDU, published 18.8, assessed 13.8, delta -5.0, recommendation flag-for-review, confidence medium. First evidence-based baseline (last_assessed null, no assessment file). No band crossing: 18.8 and 13.8 are both Critical. Routed as flag-for-review because a five-point move on a first baseline is partly a change in what has been measured rather than a change in conduct. ANTI-FALSE-POSITIVE SCREENING. All 20 entities screened. Baseline provenance was read from research/APPLIED_CHANGES.md, research/rotation-state.json and the existing assessment files before any proposal. No stale-baseline rationale was asserted against a documented recent full assessment. Five specific screens were applied and recorded. (1) VANUATU: the only in-window item is a delivery-gap commentary. The May 2026 General Assembly follow-up resolution is already priced into the published score by the applied change of 2026-05-23 and was not re-scored; re-scoring it would double-count. No new positive conduct was found, and the absence of new harm is not evidence for an upgrade, so no movement was manufactured in either direction. The assessed +1.7 against the published 41.4 is only +0.3 against the canonical reconstruction of 42.8. (2) FLORIDA: the execution record is material and is scored here for the first time, but the underlying evidence (10 executions by 15 July, DPIC record) was available at the 2026-07-19 first baseline, which cited DPIC only incidentally. Treating it as a fresh downgrade now would be assessor-to-assessor variance rather than new conduct. Held sub-threshold at -0.6 with a watch flag instead of a proposal. (3) HONG KONG: a competent response to one moderate hazard event is not a structural positive. The assessed 32.5 reproduces the 2026-07-23 baseline exactly, delta -0.3. (4) ADDIS ABABA: permitting one demonstration that aligned with the federal government’s position is not evidence of improved civic space and was not used to raise the score. (5) BOSTON DYNAMICS and UNITREE ROBOTICS: dimensions with no in-window evidence were held at values consistent with the published profile rather than re-derived from scratch, to prevent assessor variance producing a spurious delta. Boston Dynamics moved only three subdimensions (A4, E2, EQ2) on genuine in-window evidence. DIRECTIONALITY CHECK: no entity that surfaced on negative within-window evidence produced a positive proposal. ATTRIBUTION RULE APPLIED. Seven entities. ESWATINI, split decision: removal of the men from the United States is US conduct and is not scored against Eswatini; their continued detention without charge inside Eswatini and the denial of confidential legal access are Eswatini conduct and are scored. DHAKA, geographic: the 44 flood deaths occurred in southeastern Bangladesh, not Dhaka, and are not scored against the city; the police baton charge on protesting students in Dhaka is city-located conduct and is scored. ADDIS ABABA: alleged abductions and forced recruitment in Tigray are conduct of Tigray regional authorities and are not scored against Addis Ababa. JOHANNESBURG, split decision: assaults and killings by Operation Dudula and allied groups are non-state conduct and are not scored against the city; the failure to keep public clinics accessible and the absence of repair for those refused care are municipal conduct and are scored. NIGER: jihadist attacks by non-state armed groups are not scored against Niger; the arbitrary detentions and the June 2026 pretrial-detention amendment are. BOSTON DYNAMICS: the industrial dispute is between the Hyundai Motor union and Hyundai Motor, and is scored against Boston Dynamics only where the company’s own product and deployment design is implicated. KUALA LUMPUR: labour recruitment policy is federal Malaysian policy rather than Kuala Lumpur City Hall policy and is scored as sector context affecting the city. MATH HYGIENE. Canonical reconstruction (computeCompositeFromDimensions, methodology v1.2, including the integration premium term) reproduced 19 of 20 published composites exactly, maximum absolute difference 0.00. ONE GENUINE MATH-HYGIENE ISSUE FOUND. VANUATU: published composite 41.4 against a canonical reconstruction of 42.8, a difference of +1.4, outside the 0.5-point tolerance. node site/scripts/validate-indexes.mjs independently reports this as a warning and additionally reports that Vanuatu carries a composite_override while not appearing in ASSESSOR_OVERRIDE_NAMES, marking it a drift candidate. Referred for index maintenance; it is not a scoring finding and no proposal was filed on it. SUBDIMENSION QUANTISATION NOTE. Subdimension anchors are integers 1 to 5, so a dimension mean can only take multiples of 0.2. Published dimension values ending in .5 are not reproducible from five integer anchors. Where a dimension had no in-window evidence either way, its published .5 value was resolved to the nearest achievable value in the direction the evidence supports, usually the conservative lower value. This accounts for most or all of the small negative deltas on A.O. Smith (-2.2), ADP (-2.8), Aon (-3.4), Citigroup (-2.5), Apple (-1.3), Unitree Robotics (-1.5) and Agilent Technologies (0.0, where the offsetting resolution of EQU to 3.4 and INT to 3.6 produced an exact match). It is a measurement artifact, not a conduct finding. BAND OBSERVATIONS WITHOUT BAND CHANGES. Four confirmations landed in a band different from their published label while remaining inside the 5-point threshold: Dhaka assessed exactly 20.0 Critical against published 23.4 developing; Niger assessed 8.8 against published 12.5, both Critical; A.O. Smith 58.7, ADP 58.1, Aon 57.5 and Citigroup 60.0 all assessed Functional against a published established label. Because every delta is sub-threshold, band_change is recorded false and the published band stands in each case. SCANNER FEEDBACK. Three items. (1) The Unitree defect is the same failure mode flagged on 2026-07-24 and 2026-07-25: a headline claim dated to the article rather than to the event. The Pentagon designation was 8 June 2026 and the article was 20 July 2026. Date verification must extend from the source URL to the event date the summary asserts. (2) The Kuala Lumpur summary reversed the addressee of an advocacy letter, attributing to the Malaysian government a demand made of the Bangladeshi government. Directional attribution of demands should be checked against the primary report. (3) CITIGROUP was routed to rotation on a finding of no compassion-relevant evidence, but a dated in-window ruling of 24 July 2026 compelling former employees’ wage claims to arbitration was found on direct search. Recorded for scanner tuning, not as a scoring dispute. ROTATION STATE. research/rotation-state.json was updated for last_assessed, last_scanned and last_evidence_touch on all 20 entities; last_change_proposal was set only for tunis, uganda and kathmandu. composite, band and rank were left at published index values per the integrity rule. Five pre-existing rank drifts were corrected to the published index values: uganda 144 to 145, apple 64 to 59, a-o-smith 36 to 35, adp 37 to 36, aon 38 to 37. No composite or band drift was found on any assessed entity. A wider observation for index maintenance: 324 entities outside this assessment list carry a rank drift of one against the published indexes, with composite and band matching in every case. That is outside the assessor’s scope and was not touched. WATCH FLAGS SET FOR THE NEXT CYCLE. Twelve. Eswatini (whether any transferee is charged or released, and whether the arrangement enters a fifth phase), Niger (the Tiangari appeal and any application of the new four-year pretrial detention limit), Uganda (whether Nation Media Group resumes operations and whether the seized critics are produced in court), Dhaka (whether the promised make-up examinations are held and whether the baton charge is reviewed), Kathmandu (the legal basis of the detention and any prosecution of the officers involved), Kuala Lumpur (whether a binding bilateral labour agreement is negotiated and whether recruitment reopens under the syndicate structure), Addis Ababa (any Addis-specific own-conduct evidence, since this cycle found none), Tunis (the response to the 25 July rally and any further prosecutions), Johannesburg (whether clinic access is restored and enforced), Boston Dynamics (the outcome of the Ulsan dispute and any published worker-consent framework for Atlas), Unitree Robotics (the Shanghai STAR Market listing and any published misuse policy), Apple (whether a DOJ settlement is reached and what it requires), Florida (the execution pace through the remainder of 2026 and any systemic review of capital cases).
